stories.headline: Google unveils 15 billion dollars data centre investment in Malaysia
stories.script: Turning to the United States. Google announced plans on Wednesday to invest 15 billion dollars in Malaysia over the next two years to build data centres and other infrastructure as demand booms for artificial intelligence services. It said the 15 billion dollars investment will be made "over the next two years (2027 to 2028)", expanding on a 2 billion dollars investment announced in 2024.

stories.headline: Moonshot AI releases Kimi K3.1 Pro model weights
stories.script: In China. Moonshot AI has released the weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro on Hugging Face, making its flagship multimodal model available for independent deployment. The model uses a mixture-of-experts architecture with 2.8 trillion total parameters and approximately 104 billion activated per inference, and supports a context window of around one million tokens. K3.1 Pro builds on Kimi K3 with expanded reinforcement learning for coding, 3D creation, financial research and long-running agent tasks. The weights release follows the model’s earlier availability through Kimi’s applications and API. Huawei has also announced inference support through vLLM Ascend and SGLang, covering its Atlas A3 and Ascend 950 systems.

stories.headline: Activists across Europe prepare two days of protests against datacentres
stories.script: Around the world. More than 100 campaign groups will join together in 15 countries this week to call for a halt to major AI projects Protesters across Europe are planning two days of action against datacentres this week with demonstrations taking place in 15 countries. More than 100 groups are joining together for the “ Stop Dirty Data Centres ” events on Friday and Saturday. They are calling for a moratorium on large projects, citing environmental and social costs that “we can no longer afford”.

stories.headline: Nothing plans December launch for first AI-native device
stories.script: In China. Nothing plans to launch its first AI-native hardware product in December, founder and CEO Carl Pei said on November 4. Pei described the forthcoming device as a productivity tool without a screen, adding that its functions could not have been delivered through an app alone. In an essay titled “Toolmakers,” Pei argued that AI tools lack much of the context surrounding people’s work, including conversations and ideas that users do not manually enter into a chatbot. He suggested that everyday hardware could help close that gap. Nothing has not disclosed the device’s precise form, specifications or price.
stories.whyThisMatters: Nothing plans to launch its first AI-native hardware product in December, founder and CEO Carl Pei said on November 4.
keyPoints: Nothing plans December launch for first AI-native device

stories.headline: UK found to be ‘dangerously’ reliant on China for critical minerals needed for defence and AI
stories.script: Also today. Delivering net zero also at risk, say MPs as they call for centralised policy and funding for mines and diversification The UK is “dangerously” dependent on China for critical raw materials needed for the military, renewable energy infrastructure and AI, a parliamentary investigation has found. MPs on the business select committee called for an urgent centralised policy and the creation of a “critical minerals finance facility” to help fund rare earth and other critical mineral mines, and deploy grants, equity and debt to accelerate a diversification programme.
